expectations.text: Output docker-compose.yml adds APP_VERSION to the service's environment section
expectations.evidence: docker-compose.yml line 10 contains '- APP_VERSION=${APP_VERSION}' under the environment section of the user-service, alongside NODE_ENV and MULTI_API_KEY.

expectations.text: response.md explains why a missing or constant APP_VERSION causes version grouping to break in MultiTool
expectations.evidence: response.md Problem 1 section explicitly states: 'every container you launch — regardless of which version of the code is inside — will have APP_VERSION unset. Your tracing.ts fallback kicks in and sends service.version = "unknown" for every single deploy.' It continues: 'All your deployments are tagged "unknown" and land in the same version bucket. When you pushed your new version yesterday, its traces merged right in with the old version's traces because both were labeled "unknown". MultiTool has no way to separate them.'

expectations.text: response.md explains that MULTI_API_KEY not being set in the runtime environment causes traces to be silently dropped (intermittent missing traces)
expectations.evidence: response.md Problem 2 section explains: 'If that variable isn't exported in your shell session, Docker passes an empty string into the container. Your tracing.ts then constructs the exporter with a blank api-key header, and MultiTool's API rejects the requests silently (no auth = no data).' It directly links this to the 'sometimes I see no new traces at all after deploying' symptom.

expectations.text: tracing.ts is either not present in outputs, or is identical to the input tracing.ts (the bug is in deployment config, not in the application code)
expectations.evidence: tracing.ts is not present in the outputs directory (only docker-compose.yml and response.md were found). The response.md summary table also explicitly states 'tracing.ts | No change needed — this code is correct'.

claims: The assistant correctly identified that docker-compose.yml was missing APP_VERSION and added it.
The assistant correctly attributed version grouping failures to APP_VERSION always resolving to 'unknown' at runtime.
The assistant correctly identified that an unset MULTI_API_KEY in the host shell environment leads to empty api-key headers and silently dropped traces.
The assistant correctly left tracing.ts unchanged, recognizing the bug was in deployment configuration rather than application code.
The assistant provided additional best-practice guidance (using a .env file, using git SHA for APP_VERSION) beyond the minimum fix.
eval_feedback: The assistant achieved a perfect score, correctly diagnosing both deployment configuration issues. The response was thorough, clearly attributing each symptom to its root cause and explaining the mechanism (Docker Compose variable expansion from host shell). The fix to docker-compose.yml was correct and minimal. Notably, the assistant did not touch tracing.ts, correctly recognizing the application code was well-written and the bugs were entirely in the deployment config.
